index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a schematic of the SAGE system, structured into five distinct functional areas, each color-coded for clarity: platform engineering (pink), user recruitment and retention (blue), machine-based forecasting (yellow), human-computer interaction and hybridization (green), and system modeling, diagnostics, and feedback (purple). The overall layout is a left-to-right workflow, beginning with input sources on the far left and progressing through stages of data and user integration, assignment, hybrid forecasting, and final submission and scoring.

On the far left, two input streams feed into the system. The top stream consists of diverse user avatars representing human participants, which flow into a blue rounded rectangle labeled 'User Recruitment'. Below it, a second stream includes visual representations of data—binary sequences, time-series plots, and neural network diagrams—which enter a yellow rounded rectangle labeled 'Model & Data Curation'. Both streams converge into the central pink module titled 'Platform', which contains three subcomponents: 'Users & teams' (depicted as interconnected avatars), 'Models & data' (represented by stacked cylinders and images), and 'Platform Toolkit' (listing IFP Tool, Research Tool, and Interactive Tool with corresponding icons). An arrow from a pink rounded rectangle labeled 'IFP Ingest' points downward into this platform, indicating initial data ingestion.

From the platform, a dark blue arrow leads to a green rounded rectangle labeled 'IFP assignment', which shows a network diagram connecting users (avatars) to various model outputs (geometric shapes). This stage transitions into the next green module, 'HCI & Hybridization', where human avatars interact with digital interfaces (laptops, graphs) and contribute to a central icon of a musical note symbolizing a 'hybrid forecast', annotated with '~0.7' to indicate a confidence or weighting metric. This hybrid forecast is then passed to the final green module, 'Forecast submission & scoring', which represents the output phase of the system.

A horizontal purple bar at the bottom, labeled 'System Modeling, Diagnostics & Feedback', spans beneath the entire workflow and connects bidirectionally with all major modules (Platform, IFP assignment, HCI & Hybridization, and Forecast submission & scoring), indicating continuous feedback loops and system-level monitoring throughout the process. All connections between modules are represented by thick dark blue arrows, emphasizing the directional flow of information and interaction. The figure uses consistent visual attributes: rounded rectangles for modules, icons for tools and data types, and color-coding to distinguish functional domains as described in the caption.
